newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerians queue to vote in referendum.
newsitem.headline: Algerians queue to vote in referendum.

text.p: Algerians queued at polling stations early on Thursday to cast their votes in a controversial referendum on banning Moslem fundamentalists from seeking power, witnesses said from the capital Algiers.

Many voters were seen queuing outside polling stations in central Algiers, the witnesses said by telephone. Algerian state television showed polling stations opening in the southwestern town of Bechar more than an hour before voting to change the constitution was due to start at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT).
Algerians, who have endured almost five years of civil strife, have been urged by Islamic radicals and the main opposition parties to stay home or vote "No".

The draft charter for a new constitution would bar Moslem fundamentalists -- whose impending victory at the polls led the authorities to scrap a general election in 1992 -- from seeking power through the political system.

More than 60,000 people have died in conflict between Islamic radicals and the army-backed authorities since the oil-producing North African state's promised transition from one-party rule to elected parliamentary government was sidetracked.
With Moslem rebels vowing to disrupt the vote, the state has thrown out a security blanket to guard more than 35,500 polling stations in a land five times the size of France.
